claim: vLLM/SGLang pods in llm-d's precise-prefix-cache-routing guide bind their own ZMQ PUB socket (KV_EVENTS_ENDPOINT=tcp://*:5556) rather than connecting outward, so the router must be able to reach that pod's IP and port directly.
stance_target: network reachability requirements for non-k8s backends
scope_conditions: llm-d main branch guide, commit cab4b7d (2026), GPU vLLM/SGLang backends
quoted_support: each pod (vLLM or SGLang) runs with --kv-events-config '{...,"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"$(KV_EVENTS_ENDPOINT)","topic":"kv@$(POD_IP):$(POD_PORT)@<model>"}' and KV_EVENTS_ENDPOINT=tcp://*:5556, binding its own ZMQ socket.

claim: The ZMQ topic used to key KV-cache events is 'kv@<pod-ip>:<pod-port>@<model>', keyed by literal network address, not by Kubernetes pod name or UID.
stance_target: how the KV-cache indexer identifies endpoints

claim: Router-side subscription is pull/connect-initiated: each EPP router replica independently opens its own outbound ZMQ subscriber connection per discovered model-server pod, driven by kvEventsConfig.discoverPods: true registering an extractor on the data-layer 'endpoint-notification-source'.
stance_target: push vs pull KV-event subscription model
quoted_support: pod-discovery (kvEventsConfig.discoverPods: true) registers the precise-prefix-cache-producer as an extractor on the data-layer endpoint-notification-source, so each router replica installs a ZMQ subscriber per model server pod independently. All replicas converge to the same index.

claim: The GPU vLLM backend (v0.26.0+) binds a ZMQ ROUTER replay socket on port 5559 and retains the last 10,000 batches in an in-memory replay buffer, allowing a restarted router/indexer to rebuild its KV-block index without waiting for live traffic.
scope_conditions: vLLM v0.26.0+, llm-d main branch guide (2026)
quoted_support: The GPU vLLM backend (v0.26.0+) additionally binds a ZMQ ROUTER socket on port 5559 and retains the last 10,000 batches in an in-memory replay buffer for index recovery.

claim: The EPP determines which pods are eligible for KV-event subscription via the Kubernetes label llm-d.ai/guide (the InferencePool/model-server selector) — render pods deliberately omit this label so the EPP does not try to subscribe to a nonexistent KV-event socket on them.
stance_target: identity mapping between KV index and EPP endpoint name is Kubernetes-label-driven
quoted_support: These render pods deliberately do not carry the llm-d.ai/guide label -- that label is the InferencePool / model-server selector, and the EPP would otherwise treat render pods as routable model servers (and try to subscribe to their nonexistent KV-event socket).

claim: The precise-prefix-cache KV index is HA-safe across multiple router replicas because each replica converges independently via pod-discovery, but the router runs single-replica by default because in-flight token-load accounting (used by the token-load-scorer) is local per-EPP-process and not yet shared.
stance_target: router HA architecture and its dependence on pod-discovery
quoted_support: the token-load-scorer's in-flight token accounting is local to each EPP process, so two active-active replicas would each see only half the per-endpoint load and mis-gate the affinity filter. The precise KV index itself is HA-safe (each replica converges independently via pod-discovery)

claim: SGLang does not implement vLLM's render endpoints, so SGLang deployments must run a separate dedicated, GPU-less 'vllm launch render' pool to provide tokenization for precise prefix-cache routing.
scope_conditions: llm-d main branch guide (2026), SGLang backend
quoted_support: SGLang does not implement vLLM's render endpoints, so the SGLang overlay must instead run a dedicated, GPU-less vllm launch render pool (3 replicas).
